summary: Timestamp skew during canary cohort handoff causes premature pin expiry and cascading fallback/throttle
description:
Issue summary:
A NovusAI customer saw a sudden increase in fallback routing to legacy variants and token-throttling responses for pinned sessions during a staged canary roll that started 2026-02-26 03:14 UTC. The initial hypothesis is a timestamp/epoch skew between the orchestrator snapshot and edge node health probes that caused cohort handoff logic to evaluate an old snapshot as expired, forcing a pin eviction and triggering fallback routing and downstream throttling.

Impact:
- ~12% of the customer's requests in us-west experienced fallback to legacy variant, producing degraded outputs and higher per-token cost for ~45 minutes.
- Intermittent 429s observed due to fallback queues and token-bucket exhaustion on the legacy variant.
- Customer-facing sessions that were pinned to rw-open-7b-v2 returned inconsistent responses.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west) with cross-region mirror to eu-central. Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) for NovusAI. Canary rollout of rw-open-7b-v2 -> rw-open-7b-v3 (weighting scheduled 10%->30%).
- Orchestrator version: v2.13.0. Edge-proxy: v1.9.4. Serving-runtime: v4.2.1 (with qkv cache enabled).

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction):
1) Deploy a staged canary with small cohort (10% traffic) and enable prewarm probes and health-smoothing window of 30s.
2) Introduce a 2-4s system clock skew on an orchestrator replica (simulated via container time offset) while the cohort handoff snapshot is being written.
3) Send steady traffic from a pinned tenant with long-lived session tokens and mixed streaming + chat requests.
4) Observe routing decision logs for cohort assignment and pin evaluation.

Observed behavior:
- Orchestrator produced a snapshot with a publish_timestamp older than the edge node's last_seen timestamp. During cohort handoff, pin TTL checks compared publish_timestamp against edge last_seen and evaluated the pin as expired. This triggered an immediate unpin and fallback routing to legacy variant.
- Edge nodes subsequently attempted to drain and reassign, causing token revalidation storms and local token-bucket exhaustion (429s).
- A subset of sessions were re-bound to older model versions for the duration of the event.

Expected behavior:
- Pin TTL and cohort handoff should use monotonic epoch counters or consistent clock references and never treat a newer edge last_seen as evidence of an expired pin. Snapshot merges should reconcile timestamps safely across replicas.

Logs / key excerpts (sanitized):
- orchestrator[2026-02-26T03:14:12.421Z] INFO snapshot_publish id=sn-2345 publish_ts=2026-02-26T03:14:09.200Z epoch=412
- edge-proxy[2026-02-26T03:14:12.430Z] WARN pin_eval tenant=novus-team publish_ts=2026-02-26T03:14:09.200Z edge_last_seen=2026-02-26T03:14:12.400Z result=expired(reason=timestamp_lt_last_seen)
- serving-runtime[2026-02-26T03:15:01.112Z] ERROR fallback_dispatch tenant=novus-team target=legacy-variant rate_limit=throttled queue_len=120
- kv-cache[2026-02-26T03:15:02.003Z] INFO kvcache_miss tenant=novus-team key=pin:novus:session:87 status=miss
investigation_notes: SRE reproduced timestamp skew locally using container time offset; confirmed pin_evaluation uses snapshot.publish_ts and edge.last_seen naive comparison.
Hypothesis: replicas publish snapshots with host-local system time; clock skew across orchestrator replicas leads to non-monotonic publish_ts during quick successive snapshots.
Observed that pin TTL codepath lacks a monotonic epoch fallback — it treats timestamp comparison as authoritative.
No evidence of data corruption in KV store; issue stems from ordering logic during handoff/snapshot-merge.
Impact amplified by health-smoothing window: the edge considered itself newer and the orchestrator considered snapshot old, producing asymmetric view.
resolution:
Workaround applied 2026-02-26 03:30 UTC: temporarily increased pin grace window from 2s to 10s and disabled aggressive health-smoothing for affected canary cohort in us-west. Restarted two orchestrator replicas to force snapshot rewrite with consistent timestamps. Effects: pinned sessions re-bound to intended variant; 429 rate dropped to baseline within 12 minutes.

Permanent fix planned: change snapshot publish metadata to include monotonic epoch counter and make pin evaluation use epoch(major,minor) comparison before falling back to wall-clock timestamps. Add pre-deploy check that validates clock skew < 50ms between orchestrator replicas. Target rollout of fix: orchestrator v2.13.3 (ETA 2026-03-10).
follow_up_actions: ENG: implement epoch-based snapshot ordering and release orchestrator v2.13.3 (owner: @diego-alvarez, due: 2026-03-08)
SRE: add alert for snapshot_publish_ts variance > 1s across replicas in a shard (owner: @maria-chen, due: 2026-03-02)
DX: update canary runbook to include clock-skew validation step and increase default pin grace window during small cohorts (owner: @noah-kim, due: 2026-03-05)
CS: notify NovusAI with post-incident summary and include mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix (owner: @asha-raman, due: 2026-03-04)
QA: add regression test that injects clock skew into snapshot flow to validate pin stability (owner: @qa-team, due: 2026-03-09)
